intro: Colombia, named after Christopher Columbus, is the only South American country with coasts on both the Pacific and the Caribbean. It has emerged from decades of conflict.

chapters.title: El Dorado
text: The Muisca people of the highlands made fine gold objects; their ceremony of a chief covered in gold dust bathing in Lake Guatavita inspired the legend of El Dorado. The Tayrona built the Lost City (Ciudad Perdida) in the Sierra Nevada.

highlight.title: El Dorado
highlight.text: The legend of a city of gold drew Spanish explorers deep into South America.

chapters.title: New Granada
text: Spain conquered the region in the 1500s; Cartagena became a major port, fortified against pirates, and a centre of the slave trade. Bogotá was the capital of the Viceroyalty of New Granada.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Simón Bolívar won independence in 1819, creating Gran Colombia with Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama, which soon split. Panama broke away in 1903 with US support.

chapters.title: Violence and peace
text: 'La Violencia' between Liberals and Conservatives killed about 200,000 people from 1948. From the 1960s, left-wing guerrillas like the FARC, right-wing paramilitaries and drug cartels like Pablo Escobar's fought for decades. A 2016 peace deal disarmed the FARC, and President Juan Manuel Santos won the Nobel Peace Prize. Other armed groups remain active.

keyTerms.meaning: A member of an irregular armed group.
